name: Ahmanson Theatre
neighborhood: Downtown LA (The Music Center, Bunker Hill)
address: 135 N. Grand Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90012
what_it_is: The Music Center's big Broadway-style house, run by Center Theatre Group, where national tours and pre-Broadway productions play. It is one of the three CTG venues alongside the Mark Taper Forum and Kirk Douglas Theatre.
facts: Opened in 1967 as part of the Music Center complex, designed by Welton Becket & Associates, and redesigned in the mid-1990s by Ellerbe Becket to bring the balcony and mezzanine closer to the stage.
Named for the Ahmanson family of philanthropists (Howard F. Ahmanson Sr. and Caroline Leonetti Ahmanson).
December 2026: 'Oh, Mary!', the Tony-winning Broadway comedy about Mary Todd Lincoln, plays Nov 10 - Dec 6, 2026 as the 2026/27 season opener.

Dec 12, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027: 'Christmas Carol Goes Wrong', the North American premiere of the new comedy from Mischief (the company behind 'The Play That Goes Wrong'), written by Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer and Henry Shields and directed by Matt DiCarlo.
Later in the 2026/27 season: 'Fiddler on the Roof' in Yiddish (Feb 13 - Mar 14, 2027), 'Riverdance 30' (Apr 13-18, 2027) and 'BOOP! The Musical' (Jul 6 - Aug 1, 2027).
The 2026/27 season (12 productions across CTG's three venues) was announced March 30, 2026.
price: Box office prices not found; resale listings for 'Christmas Carol Goes Wrong' start around $68-$81 per ticket
booking_note: Single tickets and subscriptions sold through Center Theatre Group (centertheatregroup.org); 'Christmas Carol Goes Wrong' single tickets went on sale in August 2026

name: A Noise Within
neighborhood: East Pasadena (Foothill Blvd at Sierra Madre Villa Ave)
what_it_is: A professional classical repertory theatre company with its own permanent theatre in Pasadena, known for Shakespeare, classics and an annual holiday 'A Christmas Carol'. It describes itself as Southern California's only year-round classic repertory theatre.
facts: December 2026: 'A Christmas Carol', adapted by Geoff Elliott from Charles Dickens, runs Nov 28 - Dec 24, 2026; the holiday show is a longstanding annual tradition here (its 13th year was 2025).
No production was found for January 2027; the 2026-27 season brochure lists 'Ma Rainey's Black Bottom' as the next show in 2027, after 'Come From Away' (Oct 4 - Nov 1, 2026) and 'A Christmas Carol'.
The 2026-27 season is the company's 35th anniversary season, a six-play lineup titled 'Those Better Angels'.
Students with a valid ID can get $20 rush tickets 30 minutes before showtime, pending availability, and some performances are Pay What You Choose.
The company runs weekday student matinees performed by the same professional cast as the evening shows.
price: $20 student rush tickets (valid ID, 30 min before showtime, pending availability); Pay What You Choose for select performances
booking_note: Single tickets for the 2026-27 season went on sale June 9, 2026 via anoisewithin.org; subscribers get early access

name: The Holiday Ice Rink Pershing Square
address: 532 S. Olive St., Los Angeles, CA 90013
what_it_is: A seasonal outdoor ice skating rink set up every winter in Pershing Square, surrounded by downtown skyscrapers. It has been a DTLA holiday tradition for more than 25 years.
facts: 2026-27 season: open Thursday, Nov 12, 2026 through Sunday, Jan 3, 2027, with tickets on sale as of late October 2026.
Opening celebration and DTLA tree lighting is scheduled for Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 5-7pm, with performances, treats and the first skate of the season.
Thanksgiving week (Nov 21-29, 2026) hours are listed as 12pm - 10pm, with extended holiday-break hours from Dec 21 through Jan 3.
'Tuesdays After Dark' themed skating sessions run every Tuesday at 7:30pm.
Last season (2025-26) general admission including skate rental was $22, with $5 locker rentals and $6 skate helpers; you can also bring your own skates.
The rink marks more than 25 years of seasonal skating in Pershing Square.
price: 2026-27 prices not found; 2025-26 was $22 general admission including skate rental
hours_note: Nov 12, 2026 - Jan 3, 2027; Thanksgiving week 12pm-10pm; extended holiday-break hours Dec 21 - Jan 3 (per downtownla.com / rink site, Oct 2026)
booking_note: Buy tickets online in advance at holidayicerinkdowntownla.com; organizers strongly encourage advance online purchase

name: The Shops at Sportsmen's Lodge
neighborhood: Studio City (Ventura Blvd at Coldwater Canyon)
what_it_is: An open-air shopping and dining center built on the grounds of the old Sportsmen's Lodge event center on Ventura Boulevard. It mixes an Erewhon market, fitness, cafes and restaurants around a courtyard.
facts: A roughly $100 million redevelopment by Midwood Investment & Development with about 94,000 square feet of walkable retail, dining, fitness and communal space.
Anchored by an 11,000-square-foot Erewhon Market (the pricey LA health-food grocery famous for smoothies), which was the first tenant to open, plus an Equinox gym.
Erewhon's cafe here has floating patio decks over the courtyard.
Food options reported at the center include Sugarfish (sushi), Roberta's Pizza, HiHo Cheeseburger, Tocaya, Civil Coffee, Van Leeuwen ice cream and Tuesday's Sweet Shoppe.
Shops reported include Allbirds, Free People Movement, Vuori, SALT Optics and Madison Reed.
The neighboring Sportsmen's Lodge hotel (12825 Ventura Blvd.) closed in July 2020; the Shops are a separate development.
price: Free entry; stores and restaurants range from casual to upscale (Erewhon, Sugarfish)
hours_note: No center-wide hours found; tenants set their own (e.g. Free People Movement listed 10am-5pm Mon, 10am-8pm Tue-Fri)

name: Somemore LA
address: 2717 W. Olympic Blvd., Unit 106, Los Angeles, CA 90006
what_it_is: A teddy bear-themed dessert and drink cafe in Koreatown known for photogenic drinks and bear-shaped treats. It is a dessert cafe, not a s'mores shop, though it sells s'mores-style cookies.
facts: Drinks come in cups with teddy bear ears, heart straws and bear ice cubes, which is why it goes viral on social media.
Menu includes mille crepe cakes, bear-shaped brownies, cookies (including s'mores cookies in several flavors), macarons, matcha lattes, strawberry lattes and hot chocolate.
The bear-themed hot chocolate with a bear marshmallow is described as a crowd favorite on cooler evenings.
Reviewers single out the matcha lattes as the standout drink.
The owner and founder, Jed Jeong, started out as an architect, and the space is designed accordingly.
Follow @somemore_la on Instagram; phone (213) 529-4499.
hours_note: Listed as 12:00pm - 10:00pm, closed Tuesdays (third-party listings; one listing shows daily)

name: Dreamland Anime Cafe (Dreamland Maid Cafe)
address: 1281 E. La Habra Blvd., Unit 6, La Habra, CA 90631
what_it_is: The first permanent storefront of Dreamland Maid Cafe, an LA-born maid cafe that spent years doing pop-ups at anime conventions. It serves bubble tea and desserts with live idol shows and photos with the cast.
facts: Opened its first permanent location in La Habra in August 2026, after starting around 2020 as a Little Tokyo pop-up and touring conventions like Anime Expo, Emerald City Comic Con, MEGACON and SakuraCon.
Offers bubble tea, desserts, live idol shows ('DreamLIVE') and cheki (instant photo) sessions with the maids.
Bills itself as America's largest indie maid cafe.
At convention pop-ups, seating tickets have been $10-$15 per seat with food and drinks extra, and tickets included 1-hour seating, table-side entertainment, the idol showcase and a souvenir craft.
The cafe is cashless (mobile and card payments only).
Ran a Halloween event Oct 31, 2026 with maids in costume Oct 30 - Nov 1.
price: Convention seating tickets were $10-$15 per seat plus food and drink; La Habra storefront prices not confirmed
age_note: Convention programming described as all ages; La Habra policy not confirmed
booking_note: Convention events required reservations booked for the whole party; walk-in vs. reservation policy for the La Habra store not confirmed

name: Asayoru Maid Cafe
address: 500 N. Atlantic Blvd., Ste 125, Monterey Park, CA 91754
what_it_is: A permanent brick-and-mortar maid cafe in Monterey Park with costumed maids, live performances and Japanese-style comfort food. It calls itself LA's permanent maid cafe.
facts: Maids perform high-energy shows and interact with guests at the table, with themed comfort food and creative Japanese-style dishes.
Reviewers report it gets very busy, and one noted guests are only allowed to place one order from the menu.
Families visit: one reviewer came with a spouse and two kids, and another celebrated a birthday there.
OpenTable lists it as 'Creative Japanese' with a 4.9 rating from a small number of reviews.
hours_note: Listings conflict: OpenTable shows Thu-Sun 5-9pm; Yelp/Tripadvisor show lunch 11am-3pm plus evenings, closed Mondays (Oct 2026). Confirm before going.
booking_note: Reservations appear to go through Instagram or the cafe's own booking page (voicemail says to text on Instagram); OpenTable does not take reservations for it

name: CatCafe Lounge
neighborhood: Venice (Washington Blvd near the Venice / Marina del Rey border)
what_it_is: LA's first nonprofit cat cafe, where you book a timed session to hang out with dozens of adoptable rescue cats. It moved from West LA to Venice Beach in early 2026.
facts: A typical visit is a 70-minute lounge session with roughly 20-30 adoptable cats.
It is a nonprofit rescue: cats you meet can be adopted, and the organization reports having saved more than 2,000 cats.
Rising rent pushed it out of its old West LA location (1736 S. Sepulveda Blvd.); supporters raised about $38,000 in two weeks to fund the move.
Reopened in Venice on Feb 21, 2026, with a grand opening celebration on March 28, 2026.
The old location had an outdoor 'catio' and hosted events like reading to cats.
An older report listed a $75 same-day adoption fee (may have changed).
booking_note: Reservations are made online through the cafe's booking page for weekday and weekend sessions

name: Anteiku Cafe
address: 14911 Pacific Ave., Unit 100, Baldwin Park, CA 91706
what_it_is: A small anime-inspired coffee shop in Baldwin Park named after the cafe in 'Tokyo Ghoul'. It serves themed matcha lattes, coffee and Japanese snacks in anime-decorated space.
facts: Named after Anteiku, the coffee shop in 'Tokyo Ghoul'; reviewers reference the character Kaneki and the show's vibe.
Known for anime-themed drinks like 'Nezuko's Love Matcha' (a Demon Slayer-inspired matcha latte) and matcha lattes with banana creme.
Also serves food like onigiri (two pieces per order), which reviewers praise.
Featured in a September 2025 SAC Media story as bringing anime and coffee culture to Baldwin Park.
A flag outside the shop catches people's eye while driving by.
hours_note: Unclaimed listing shows roughly 8:30am-5pm Mon-Thu and Sun, extended to 7pm Fri-Sat; confirm before visiting
